description:
Fixture 01174's oracle prints `Enum.uniq(%{a: 1, b: 1})` and `Enum.uniq_by(%{a: 1, b: 1}, ...)`. Elixir 1.19.4 / OTP 28 enumerates a small atom-keyed map in an order that is not defined: the same `elixir -e 'IO.inspect(Enum.to_list(%{a: 1, b: 1}))'` printed `[b: 1, a: 1]` once in three runs. CI stays green only because the stored stamp means Elixir never starts; `ORACLE=regen` rewrote 01174's golden to `{[], [b: 1, a: 1], [b: 1]}` on one run, and `ORACLE=check` can fail the same way.

Done when: 01174 enumerates an input whose order Elixir defines (a keyword list, or a map with integer keys), regenerated through the oracle; every other oracle fixture that enumerates an atom-keyed map literal is checked and fixed the same way; two consecutive `ORACLE=check` runs agree.

comments.text: Seen again 2026-11-17 by Bugs and Cleanup (building fz-9x7.31): local Elixir 1.19.4 / OTP 28 regenerates 01174's last golden line as {[], [b: 1, a: 1], [b: 1]} where the stamped golden (CI pins Elixir 1.19.5 / OTP 28.5.0.1, .github/workflows/ci.yml:37-38) has {[], [a: 1, b: 1], [a: 1]}. The default run never sees it because the stamp matches the file. Local and CI Elixir versions differ (1.19.4 vs 1.19.5).

title: Fixture 01174's oracle depends on Elixir's order for an atom-keyed map
